finding: A source-first `batch checkpoint` invocation can mutate the queue-head task close state and stage close artifacts, then fail later when the batch runner tries to auto-claim the next task through a source-first lifecycle write guard. The command is therefore not atomic from the operator's perspective.
expectedBehavior: Batch checkpoint should either preflight all post-close lifecycle writes before mutating the queue head, or complete the close and stop with a deliberate checkpoint-complete/next-claim-deferred result. It must not leave operators to infer whether the close succeeded after a later source-first refusal.
evidenceOrRepro: Original incident: after a source-first batch checkpoint, TASK-GIT-0026 was closed and close artifacts were staged, then the command returned `ATM_SOURCE_FIRST_WRITE_REFUSED` while attempting the next claim. Current verification on 2026-09-02: `packages/cli/src/commands/batch/checkpoint-commit-window-policy.test.ts` passed and asserts the checkpoint implementation contains no `await runNext`, creates a pending commit window after close, and blocks resume while that window is dirty. `tests/cli/batch-checkpoint-runner-sync-recovery.test.ts` and `tests/cli/batch-done-task-pruning.test.ts` also passed, covering recovery routing and terminal queue-head pruning.
followUp: Closed. Retain the checkpoint commit-window and runner-sync recovery regressions in the batch validation set.
